taxon:

description: KdpA (CCNA_01663) is the potassium-selective membrane subunit of the high-affinity KdpABC
  uptake system in Caulobacter vibrioides NA1000. Native deletion and fitness experiments establish the
  KdpABC system as an important contributor to growth under potassium limitation. Conserved KdpA signatures
  and curated homology support potassium recognition and delivery to the coupled KdpB ATPase; this subunit-level
  mechanism has not been reconstituted with the NA1000 complex. KdpA does not supply the ATP-hydrolyzing
  catalytic center. Kup and other uptake capacity permit residual growth when Kdp is absent.

    id: GO:0005886
    label: plasma membrane
  evidence_type: IEA

  - UniProtKB-SubCell:SL-0037
  - PANTHER:PTN000770087
  - UniRule:UR000058579
  review:
    summary: kdpA is an inner-membrane component of the KdpABC pump.
    action: ACCEPT
    reason: The target record supplies curated HAMAP membrane localization and transmembrane features.
      Native potassium-dependent KdpABC genetics corroborates pump function; membrane placement is inferred
      from sequence and conserved architecture rather than a NA1000 localization assay.
    supported_by:

      supporting_text: Cell inner membrane
- term:
    id: GO:0006813

  qualifier: involved_in
  supporting_entities:
  - InterPro:IPR004623

  review:
    summary: kdpA participates in potassium transport across the plasma membrane.
    action: MODIFY
    reason: The general potassium transport term is true. GO:0071805, already present in this review,
      specifies the transmembrane movement performed by the KdpABC machinery. The native locus phenotype
      and conserved subunit function support this refinement; no isolated-subunit transport assay is claimed.
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:39133005
      supporting_text: both Δ kdpABC and Δ kdpDE mutants had a growth delay at limiting but not at abundant
        K + concentration
    - reference_id: file:CAUVN/kdpA/kdpA-uniprot.txt
      record_section: ["CC:FUNCTION"]
      supporting_text: This subunit binds the periplasmic potassium ions and delivers the ions to the
        membrane domain of KdpB through an intramembrane tunnel.
    proposed_replacement_terms:
    - id: GO:0071805
      label: potassium ion transmembrane transport
- term:
    id: GO:0008556
    label: P-type potassium transmembrane transporter activity

      ATP hydrolysis. The molecular-function claim is retained in its assembled-complex context and synthesized
      as a contribution, not as autonomous ATPase activity. Target KdpA signatures and native KdpABC genetics
      support the conserved role.
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: file:CAUVN/kdpA/kdpA-uniprot.txt
      record_section: ["CC:FUNCTION"]
      supporting_text: This subunit binds the periplasmic potassium ions and delivers the ions to the
        membrane domain of KdpB through an intramembrane tunnel.
    - reference_id: PMID:39133005
      supporting_text: both Δ kdpABC and Δ kdpDE mutants had a growth delay at limiting but not at abundant
        K + concentration
- term:
    id: GO:0030955
    label: potassium ion binding
  evidence_type: IEA
  original_reference_id: GO_REF:0000104
  qualifier: enables
  supporting_entities:
  - UniRule:UR000058579
  review:
    summary: KdpA recognizes potassium as the substrate of the uptake complex.

    supported_by:
    - reference_id: file:CAUVN/kdpA/kdpA-uniprot.txt
      record_section: ["CC:FUNCTION"]
      supporting_text: This subunit binds the periplasmic potassium ions and delivers the ions to the
        membrane domain of KdpB through an intramembrane tunnel.
- term:
    id: GO:0071805
    label: potassium ion transmembrane transport
  evidence_type: IEA
  original_reference_id: GO_REF:0000118
  qualifier: involved_in
  supporting_entities:

  review:
    summary: kdpA contributes to the KdpABC potassium import machinery.
    action: ACCEPT
    reason: Native NA1000 KdpABC deletion and fitness experiments support a role in potassium uptake under
      limiting conditions. The subunit-specific contribution follows the verified Kdp family architecture
      and curated sequence features, not an assumption that growth impairment measures purified transport

    supported_by:

    - reference_id: file:CAUVN/kdpA/kdpA-uniprot.txt
      record_section: ["CC:FUNCTION"]
      supporting_text: This subunit binds the periplasmic potassium ions and delivers the ions to the
        membrane domain of KdpB through an intramembrane tunnel.

description: KdpD (CCNA_01666) is a membrane-associated histidine-kinase-family regulator of the KdpE
  response regulator in Caulobacter vibrioides NA1000. Native deletion, complementation, point-mutant
  and promoter-reporter experiments support both positive and negative control, with a proposed kinase
  contribution during early exponential growth and a predominant KdpE-directed phosphatase role later
  in potassium-limited cultures. These catalytic assignments are inferred from genetics rather than purified
  NA1000 phosphotransfer or dephosphorylation measurements. KdpE-dependent transcription persists without
  KdpD, suggesting another phosphorylation source whose identity is unresolved. The protein lacks the
  recognizable GAF domain found in Escherichia coli KdpD; a conserved motif-based proposal for serine-kinase
  regulation of KdpB has not been tested in NA1000.

document.description: KdpD (CCNA_01666) is a membrane-associated histidine-kinase-family regulator of the KdpE response regulator in Caulobacter vibrioides NA1000. Native deletion, complementation, point-mutant and promoter-reporter experiments support both positive and negative control, with a proposed kinase contribution during early exponential growth and a predominant KdpE-directed phosphatase role later in potassium-limited cultures. These catalytic assignments are inferred from genetics rather than purified NA1000 phosphotransfer or dephosphorylation measurements. KdpE-dependent transcription persists without KdpD, suggesting another phosphorylation source whose identity is unresolved. The protein lacks the recognizable GAF domain found in Escherichia coli KdpD; a conserved motif-based proposal for serine-kinase regulation of KdpB has not been tested in NA1000.

review.summary: KdpD is a sensor histidine-kinase-family regulator with a proposed early-growth kinase contribution.
review.reason: The target HisKA/HATPase architecture and native His670/Phe832 mutant, complementation and reporter data support a histidine-kinase signaling role. PMID:39133005 infers the catalytic balance from genetics, and KdpD is not required for all KdpE activation. Acceptance does not assert an exclusive cognate phosphorylation source or direct purified kinase kinetics.

description: KdpB is the P-type ATPase subunit of the potassium uptake system in Nitratidesulfovibrio
  vulgaris Hildenborough. Its nucleotide-binding and phosphorylation domains couple ATP hydrolysis through
  an aspartyl-phosphate intermediate to potassium translocation by the assembled membrane complex. The
  KdpB subunit provides the energy-coupling machinery and cytoplasmic ion-release site, working with the
  potassium-selective KdpA subunit and the KdpC accessory component.

document.description: KdpB is the P-type ATPase subunit of the potassium uptake system in Nitratidesulfovibrio vulgaris Hildenborough. Its nucleotide-binding and phosphorylation domains couple ATP hydrolysis through an aspartyl-phosphate intermediate to potassium translocation by the assembled membrane complex. The KdpB subunit provides the energy-coupling machinery and cytoplasmic ion-release site, working with the potassium-selective KdpA subunit and the KdpC accessory component.

description: 'KdpA is the potassium-binding and potassium-translocating subunit of KdpFABC, the inducible
  high-affinity ATP-driven potassium uptake pump of the bacterial inner membrane, which is expressed
  when external K+ falls to micromolar levels. KdpA is a ten-transmembrane-helix member of the superfamily

  show an intramembrane tunnel that carries K+ from the KdpA selectivity filter to the canonical
  cation site of KdpB, with the accessory single-span subunits KdpC and KdpF stabilizing the complex.'

document.description: KdpA is the potassium-binding and potassium-translocating subunit of KdpFABC, the inducible high-affinity ATP-driven potassium uptake pump of the bacterial inner membrane, which is expressed when external K+ falls to micromolar levels. KdpA is a ten-transmembrane-helix member of the superfamily of potassium transporters (SKT), built from four M1PM2 repeats around a KcsA-like selectivity filter that binds dehydrated K+ and confers the high affinity and K+/Rb+ discrimination of the system. KdpA itself has no ATPase activity: energy is supplied by the P-type ATPase subunit KdpB, and structures show an intramembrane tunnel that carries K+ from the KdpA selectivity filter to the canonical cation site of KdpB, with the accessory single-span subunits KdpC and KdpF stabilizing the complex.

description: 'KdpB is the catalytic P-type ATPase subunit (type IA, EC 7.2.2.6) of KdpFABC, the high-affinity,
  ATP-driven potassium uptake system of the E. coli inner membrane that is expressed under K+ limitation
  under control of the KdpD/KdpE two-component system. KdpB binds Mg-ATP in its cytoplasmic N and P domains
  and forms a phosphoenzyme on Asp307 of the DKTGT motif, cycling through E1/E2 conformations while KdpA,
  KdpC and KdpF remain static. ATP hydrolysis by KdpB is coupled to K+ uptake: K+ is selected by the channel-like
  KdpA subunit, passes through an intramembrane tunnel to binding sites in the KdpB transmembrane domain,
  and is released by KdpB to the cytoplasm. At high K+, the N-terminal atypical serine kinase of KdpD
  phosphorylates KdpB Ser162 in the A-domain TGES motif and inhibits the pump.'

document.description: KdpB is the catalytic P-type ATPase subunit (type IA, EC 7.2.2.6) of KdpFABC, the high-affinity, ATP-driven potassium uptake system of the E. coli inner membrane that is expressed under K+ limitation under control of the KdpD/KdpE two-component system. KdpB binds Mg-ATP in its cytoplasmic N and P domains and forms a phosphoenzyme on Asp307 of the DKTGT motif, cycling through E1/E2 conformations while KdpA, KdpC and KdpF remain static. ATP hydrolysis by KdpB is coupled to K+ uptake: K+ is selected by the channel-like KdpA subunit, passes through an intramembrane tunnel to binding sites in the KdpB transmembrane domain, and is released by KdpB to the cytoplasm. At high K+, the N-terminal atypical serine kinase of KdpD phosphorylates KdpB Ser162 in the A-domain TGES motif and inhibits the pump.

description: KdpC is a single-pass accessory subunit of the E. coli KdpFABC high-affinity ATP-driven
  potassium uptake pump. Its soluble domain lies in the periplasm and contacts KdpA near the selectivity-filter
  entrance. KdpC contributes to pump function as an associated structural component, although the
  exact effect of its periplasmic domain on ion entry or complex stability remains unresolved. ATP
  hydrolysis and cytoplasmic ion release occur in KdpB; K+ selection and entry occur in KdpA. Historical
  isolated-domain biochemistry suggested ATP-dependent interaction with KdpB, but the proposed cytoplasmic
  catalytic-chaperone arrangement conflicts with intact-complex topology.

document.description: KdpC is a single-pass accessory subunit of the E. coli KdpFABC high-affinity ATP-driven potassium uptake pump. Its soluble domain lies in the periplasm and contacts KdpA near the selectivity-filter entrance. KdpC contributes to pump function as an associated structural component, although the exact effect of its periplasmic domain on ion entry or complex stability remains unresolved. ATP hydrolysis and cytoplasmic ion release occur in KdpB; K+ selection and entry occur in KdpA. Historical isolated-domain biochemistry suggested ATP-dependent interaction with KdpB, but the proposed cytoplasmic catalytic-chaperone arrangement conflicts with intact-complex topology.

Removal does not dispute that the subunits associate.

core_functions.description: KdpC contributes to ATP-driven K+ uptake as an accessory structural subunit of KdpFABC. Its single transmembrane helix and periplasmic domain contact the complex near the KdpA selectivity-filter entrance; a stabilizing role is proposed, while the precise effect on ion entry or assembly remains unresolved. It is not assigned an independent ATPase activity.

suggested_questions.question: How can the reported ATP binding and KdpB nucleotide-affinity effect of KdpC be reconciled with the periplasmic location of its soluble domain in all KdpFABC structures?

  label: Escherichia coli K-12
description: KdpD is the inner-membrane sensor of the E. coli KdpD/KdpE two-component system
  that controls the high-affinity K+ uptake pump KdpFABC. The 894-residue homodimer has a
  large cytoplasmic N-terminal input region (containing a Walker A/B atypical kinase domain
  and a Usp domain), four transmembrane helices, and a cytoplasmic C-terminal transmitter
  (GAF, DHp and HATPase_c domains). Under K+ limitation or salt stress KdpD autophosphorylates
  His673 in trans and transfers the phosphoryl group to KdpE, which then activates kdpFABC
  transcription; it also dephosphorylates KdpE~P, and the kinase/phosphatase balance responds
  to both extracellular and intracellular K+. Its activity is modulated by UspC (scaffold
  under salt stress) and dephosphorylated IIA(Ntr). At high K+ the N-terminal atypical serine
  kinase domain phosphorylates KdpB Ser162, inhibiting the KdpFABC pump post-translationally.

document.description: KdpD is the inner-membrane sensor of the E. coli KdpD/KdpE two-component system that controls the high-affinity K+ uptake pump KdpFABC. The 894-residue homodimer has a large cytoplasmic N-terminal input region (containing a Walker A/B atypical kinase domain and a Usp domain), four transmembrane helices, and a cytoplasmic C-terminal transmitter (GAF, DHp and HATPase_c domains). Under K+ limitation or salt stress KdpD autophosphorylates His673 in trans and transfers the phosphoryl group to KdpE, which then activates kdpFABC transcription; it also dephosphorylates KdpE~P, and the kinase/phosphatase balance responds to both extracellular and intracellular K+. Its activity is modulated by UspC (scaffold under salt stress) and dephosphorylated IIA(Ntr). At high K+ the N-terminal atypical serine kinase domain phosphorylates KdpB Ser162, inhibiting the KdpFABC pump post-translationally.

description: KdpE is the cytoplasmic OmpR/PhoB-family response regulator of the E. coli KdpD/KdpE
  two-component system. It has an N-terminal receiver domain phosphorylated on Asp52 by the
  sensor kinase KdpD (and by PhoR in the absence of KdpD) and a C-terminal winged helix-turn-helix
  DNA-binding domain. Phosphorylated KdpE dimerizes via the alpha4-beta5-alpha5 face of its
  receiver domain and binds two AT-rich 6-bp half-sites upstream of the kdpFABC promoter,
  activating transcription of the high-affinity K+ uptake pump KdpFABC under K+ limitation
  or salt stress. KdpD is the phosphatase that returns KdpE~P to the inactive state.

document.description: KdpE is the cytoplasmic OmpR/PhoB-family response regulator of the E. coli KdpD/KdpE two-component system. It has an N-terminal receiver domain phosphorylated on Asp52 by the sensor kinase KdpD (and by PhoR in the absence of KdpD) and a C-terminal winged helix-turn-helix DNA-binding domain. Phosphorylated KdpE dimerizes via the alpha4-beta5-alpha5 face of its receiver domain and binds two AT-rich 6-bp half-sites upstream of the kdpFABC promoter, activating transcription of the high-affinity K+ uptake pump KdpFABC under K+ limitation or salt stress. KdpD is the phosphatase that returns KdpE~P to the inactive state.

description: KdpF is a 29-residue, N-formylated, single-pass transmembrane peptide encoded as the first
  gene of the kdpFABC operon and a subunit of the KdpFABC high-affinity ATP-driven potassium uptake complex
  of the E. coli inner membrane. Structures show KdpF as one transmembrane helix at the KdpA-KdpB interface
  that remains static during the catalytic cycle. In the tested deletion conditions, KdpF is dispensable
  for growth at 0.1 mM K+ and membrane-bound ATPase activity is nearly unchanged, whereas its absence
  greatly reduces activity of the purified detergent-solubilised complex, where it can be replaced by
  added lipids; it therefore acts as a structural stabilising element of the pump rather than a catalytic
  subunit.

document.description: KdpF is a 29-residue, N-formylated, single-pass transmembrane peptide encoded as the first gene of the kdpFABC operon and a subunit of the KdpFABC high-affinity ATP-driven potassium uptake complex of the E. coli inner membrane. Structures show KdpF as one transmembrane helix at the KdpA-KdpB interface that remains static during the catalytic cycle. In the tested deletion conditions, KdpF is dispensable for growth at 0.1 mM K+ and membrane-bound ATPase activity is nearly unchanged, whereas its absence greatly reduces activity of the purified detergent-solubilised complex, where it can be replaced by added lipids; it therefore acts as a structural stabilising element of the pump rather than a catalytic subunit.

description: KdpA (PP_4161) is the potassium-selective entry subunit of the high-affinity KdpFABC

  transfer and release into the cytoplasm. The kdp locus couples this pump to KdpD/KdpE regulation.

document.description: KdpA (PP_4161) is the potassium-selective entry subunit of the high-affinity KdpFABC uptake pump in the Pseudomonas putida KT2440 inner membrane. Its ten-helix transporter architecture includes a KcsA-like selectivity filter with a TNGGG motif. By homology with structurally and biochemically characterized Escherichia coli KdpFABC, KdpA captures periplasmic potassium and delivers it through an intramembrane tunnel to KdpB, whose ATPase cycle drives transfer and release into the cytoplasm. The kdp locus couples this pump to KdpD/KdpE regulation.

review.summary: Integral inner (plasma) membrane location of the KdpA transport subunit, from the HAMAP KdpA rule.
review.reason: KdpA is a ten-helix polytopic membrane protein; the E. coli ortholog is experimentally located in the inner membrane and the PSEPK sequence retains the predicted ten-helix topology.

The target KdpA family signatures and conserved filter support this contribution by homology to E. coli, including the functional tunnel tests in PMID:41259220. description: 'KdpB (PP_4160, kdpFABC operon) is the catalytic P-type ATPase subunit (type IA, EC 7.2.2.6)
  of the KdpFABC high-affinity ATP-driven potassium uptake complex in the inner membrane of Pseudomonas

  and couples ATP hydrolysis to K+ uptake: K+ is selected by the channel-like KdpA subunit, transferred
  through an intramembrane tunnel to sites in the KdpB transmembrane domain, and released by KdpB to the
  cytoplasm.'

document.description: KdpB (PP_4160, kdpFABC operon) is the catalytic P-type ATPase subunit (type IA, EC 7.2.2.6) of the KdpFABC high-affinity ATP-driven potassium uptake complex in the inner membrane of Pseudomonas putida KT2440. By orthology with the characterised Escherichia coli enzyme, it binds Mg-ATP in its cytoplasmic N and P domains, forms an aspartyl-phosphate intermediate on the conserved DKTGT aspartate (Asp311 here), and couples ATP hydrolysis to K+ uptake: K+ is selected by the channel-like KdpA subunit, transferred through an intramembrane tunnel to sites in the KdpB transmembrane domain, and released by KdpB to the cytoplasm.

document.description: KdpC (PP_4159) is a single-pass accessory subunit of the Pseudomonas putida KT2440 high-affinity KdpFABC potassium pump. Its KdpC-family architecture supports a periplasmic domain contacting KdpA and a structural contribution to the assembled transporter, inferred from Escherichia coli structures. KdpA selects potassium and delivers it to KdpB, which drives ion transfer and cytoplasmic release through its ATPase cycle.

review.summary: The physiological ATP-binding claim is unresolved for KT2440 KdpC.
review.reason: The full E. coli PMID:21711450 study reports photoaffinity-labeling and ATP-dependent isolated-domain interaction, but direct ITC did not detect ATP binding to isolated KdpC up to 2.8 mM ATP. These observations are retained rather than treated as a negative across all conditions. Later intact-complex structures place its soluble domain in the periplasm, challenging the proposed cytoplasmic catalytic-chaperone mechanism without disproving all binding. No KT2440 assay resolves this transfer; topology and another subunit binding ATP are insufficient grounds to dismiss the original biochemical observations.

description: 'KdpD (PP_4158; Q88FD9) is the predicted inner-membrane sensor histidine kinase of the KdpD/KdpE
  two-component system of Pseudomonas putida KT2440, encoded next to kdpE and the kdpFABC operon for the

  orthology with E. coli KdpD it autophosphorylates and phosphorylates KdpE in response to K+ limitation,
  and likely also dephosphorylates KdpE~P.'

document.description: KdpD (PP_4158; Q88FD9) is the predicted inner-membrane sensor histidine kinase of the KdpD/KdpE two-component system of Pseudomonas putida KT2440, encoded next to kdpE and the kdpFABC operon for the high-affinity K+ uptake pump. It has the full-length KdpD architecture: a cytoplasmic N-terminal KdpD domain and Usp domain, four transmembrane helices, and a cytoplasmic HisKA/HATPase_c transmitter. By orthology with E. coli KdpD it autophosphorylates and phosphorylates KdpE in response to K+ limitation, and likely also dephosphorylates KdpE~P.

document.description: KdpE (PP_4157; Q88FE0) is the predicted OmpR/PhoB-family response regulator of the KdpD/KdpE two-component system of Pseudomonas putida KT2440, encoded next to kdpD. It has an N-terminal receiver domain with the phosphorylatable Asp55 and a C-terminal OmpR/PhoB winged helix-turn-helix DNA-binding domain. By orthology with E. coli KdpE, phosphorylation by KdpD activates KdpE to bind the cis-regulatory sequence upstream of the kdpFABC promoter and activate transcription of the high-affinity K+ uptake pump KdpFABC.

family_id: PANTHER:PTHR30607
family_name: POTASSIUM-TRANSPORTING ATPASE A CHAIN
preferred_name: KdpA potassium-binding and translocating subunit of KdpFABC
summary: >-
  KdpA is the potassium-selective, membrane-embedded subunit of the KdpFABC
  high-affinity potassium uptake complex found in many bacteria and some
  archaea. It belongs to the superfamily of K+ transporters (SKT) and carries a
  channel-like selectivity filter formed by four M1-P-M2 repeats. KdpA binds
  periplasmic K+ and passes it through an intramembrane tunnel to the
  membrane domain of the P-type ATPase subunit KdpB, which releases it into the
  cytoplasm at the expense of ATP. KdpA does not hydrolyse ATP itself: the
  complete reaction of P-type potassium transport is a property of the
  assembled KdpFABC complex, to which KdpA contributes substrate selection and
  translocation.
functional_coherence: COHERENT
coherence_reason: >-
  PANTHER resolves a single subfamily (SF2) and a single PAINT node for this
  family. Every reviewed member is annotated as KdpA of a Kdp operon, and the
  selectivity-filter architecture is shared. There are no known divergent
  paralog groups; the main interpretive caution is that the transporter
  activity is a complex-level activity to which KdpA contributes.

document.preferred_name: KdpA potassium-binding and translocating subunit of KdpFABC
document.summary: KdpA is the potassium-selective, membrane-embedded subunit of the KdpFABC high-affinity potassium uptake complex found in many bacteria and some archaea. It belongs to the superfamily of K+ transporters (SKT) and carries a channel-like selectivity filter formed by four M1-P-M2 repeats. KdpA binds periplasmic K+ and passes it through an intramembrane tunnel to the membrane domain of the P-type ATPase subunit KdpB, which releases it into the cytoplasm at the expense of ATP. KdpA does not hydrolyse ATP itself: the complete reaction of P-type potassium transport is a property of the assembled KdpFABC complex, to which KdpA contributes substrate selection and translocation.
document.coherence_reason: PANTHER resolves a single subfamily (SF2) and a single PAINT node for this family. Every reviewed member is annotated as KdpA of a Kdp operon, and the selectivity-filter architecture is shared. There are no known divergent paralog groups; the main interpretive caution is that the transporter activity is a complex-level activity to which KdpA contributes.

family_id: PANTHER:PTHR43743
family_name: POTASSIUM-TRANSPORTING ATPASE ATP-BINDING SUBUNIT
preferred_name: KdpB P-type ATPase subunit of KdpFABC
summary: >-
  KdpB is the catalytic, pump-like subunit of the KdpFABC high-affinity
  potassium uptake complex of bacteria and some archaea. It is a type IA
  member of the P-type ATPase superfamily, with seven transmembrane helices and
  the phosphorylation (P), nucleotide-binding (N) and actuator (A) cytoplasmic
  domains. ATP hydrolysis proceeds through a 4-aspartylphosphate intermediate
  in the P domain; the energy is coupled to release of K+ that the
  channel-like subunit KdpA delivers through an intramembrane tunnel. In E.
  coli, phosphorylation of a serine in the KdpB A domain (Ser162) inhibits the
  complex. KdpB orthologs are confined to Kdp systems, so the family is a
  reliable marker of KdpFABC.
functional_coherence: COHERENT
coherence_reason: >-
  The KdpB-specific family and its SF1 retain the P-type ATPase catalytic architecture in Kdp systems.
  KdpB contributes Mg-ATP hydrolysis, ion receipt from KdpA and cytoplasmic release to the assembled pump.
  E. coli Ser162 regulatory phosphorylation is an experimentally grounded member feature, not a measured
  universal property of every family member.

family_name: SENSOR PROTEIN KDPD
preferred_name: KdpD regulatory proteins with variable histidine- and serine-kinase architectures
summary: >-
  KdpD proteins regulate potassium uptake through variable domain architectures. Canonical full-length
  E. coli KdpD combines an N-terminal KdpD domain and Usp region, four transmembrane helices, a GAF region,
  and a C-terminal histidine-kinase transmitter. Its histidine phosphorelay controls KdpE-dependent transcription,
  while a distinct N-terminal atypical serine kinase inhibits the KdpFABC pump through KdpB phosphorylation.
  Short KdpD/Usp proteins can retain the serine-kinase mechanism while lacking the histidine transmitter;
  the experimentally studied Deinococcus geothermalis form is regulated by c-di-AMP. Domain presence,
  regulatory input and membrane association cannot be assumed uniform throughout the family.
functional_coherence: MOSTLY_COHERENT
coherence_reason: >-
  SF1 combines full-length histidine-kinase-containing proteins and short N-terminal KdpD architectures.
  P73870 and Q725T9 lack the canonical histidine transmitter based on domain/signature architecture, not
  merely length; this does not establish absence of serine-kinase activity. Q1J2K3 is an independently
  verified SF1 member and the short D. geothermalis ASK comparator in PMID38622146. A single subfamily
  does not separate all activity and topology classes.

interpro/panther/PTHR48111/PTHR48111-rev.text:
family_id: PANTHER:PTHR48111
family_name: REGULATOR OF RPOS
preferred_name: OmpR/PhoB-type winged-helix response regulators
summary: >-
  A large family of two-component response regulators with an N-terminal
  receiver domain and a C-terminal winged helix-turn-helix (OmpR/PhoB-type)
  DNA-binding output domain. Phosphotransfer from a cognate sensor histidine
  kinase to a conserved receiver aspartate drives dimerization and binding to
  promoter regions, so that each regulator controls the regulon of its own
  signalling pathway. Characterized members include E. coli OmpR, PhoB, PhoP,
  CpxR, ArcA, BaeR, BasR, CreB, TorR and KdpE, Pseudomonas AlgR and
  streptococcal WalR. The receiver-to-DNA-binding mechanism is shared, but
  regulon, target promoters, regulatory sign and physiological process are
  set by the subfamily.
functional_coherence: MOSTLY_COHERENT
coherence_reason: >-
  The receiver-domain phosphorelay activity, cis-regulatory DNA binding and
  transcriptional regulation are shared family-wide and supported by many
  seeds in PANTHER's 49 subfamilies. Specific biology is not shared: KdpE
  (SF50) activates the kdpFABC potassium-pump operon, OmpR (SF4) is a dual
  activator and repressor of porin genes, ArcA (SF55) controls aerobic
  respiration genes, and so on. The direction of regulation and any process
  more specific than transcription regulation must therefore be assigned per
  subfamily.

document.summary: A large family of two-component response regulators with an N-terminal receiver domain and a C-terminal winged helix-turn-helix (OmpR/PhoB-type) DNA-binding output domain. Phosphotransfer from a cognate sensor histidine kinase to a conserved receiver aspartate drives dimerization and binding to promoter regions, so that each regulator controls the regulon of its own signalling pathway. Characterized members include E. coli OmpR, PhoB, PhoP, CpxR, ArcA, BaeR, BasR, CreB, TorR and KdpE, Pseudomonas AlgR and streptococcal WalR. The receiver-to-DNA-binding mechanism is shared, but regulon, target promoters, regulatory sign and physiological process are set by the subfamily.
document.coherence_reason: The receiver-domain phosphorelay activity, cis-regulatory DNA binding and transcriptional regulation are shared family-wide and supported by many seeds in PANTHER's 49 subfamilies. Specific biology is not shared: KdpE (SF50) activates the kdpFABC potassium-pump operon, OmpR (SF4) is a dual activator and repressor of porin genes, ArcA (SF55) controls aerobic respiration genes, and so on. The direction of regulation and any process more specific than transcription regulation must therefore be assigned per subfamily.

module.text:
id: MODULE:bacterial_kdp_potassium_homeostasis
title: Bacterial Kdp potassium uptake and regulatory control
description: A bacterial potassium-homeostasis module combining the KdpABC transport machinery, a variably
  required KdpF stabilizing component, and lineage-dependent control of pump production and activity.
  KdpA selects potassium and supplies the inter-subunit pathway; KdpB couples ATP turnover to ion transfer
  and cytoplasmic release, supported by KdpC. Canonical KdpD-to-KdpE signaling induces pump expression,
  whereas a Caulobacter regulatory profile retains KdpE output without making cognate KdpD activation
  obligatory. Characterized KdpD proteins can also restrain KdpE phosphorylation or inhibit existing pumps
  through KdpB serine phosphorylation. Other potassium uptake systems and non-Kdp virulence outputs are
  outside this module.

scope: CONCRETE

- &id001
  source_id: PMID:33798529
  title: Molecular Mechanisms for Bacterial Potassium Homeostasis.
  statement: Comparative review distinguishes the ATP-driven Kdp pump from other potassium systems and
    separates KdpF stabilization from KdpC topology.
  supporting_text: KdpC is a subunit of unassigned classification, consisting of a single transmembrane
    helix and a periplasmic soluble domain
- &id004
  source_id: PMID:31259644
  title: The KdpFABC complex - K(+) transport against all odds.
  statement: Comparative review identifies KdpF as a variable stabilizing component, rather than a universal
    requirement for transport.
  supporting_text: Although KdpF is absent in a significant number of bacterial genomes and is not essential
    for activity of the E. coli complex
- &id012
  source_id: PMID:17536175
  title: The Kdp-ATPase system and its regulation.
  statement: Bacterial kdpABC architecture is more conserved than its associated regulatory gene arrangement.
  supporting_text: 'the kdpA, kdpB

    and kdpC is relatively fixed but the kdpD/E genes show different arrangements in

    distantly related bacteria'
- source_id: PMID:14604015
  title: The roles and regulation of potassium in bacteria.
  statement: Bacteria commonly use multiple independent potassium uptake systems with different kinetics
    and regulation.
  supporting_text: 'In most species two or more independent saturable K(+)-transport

    systems are present.'
- &id003
  source_id: PMID:10608856
  title: The KdpF subunit is part of the K(+)-translocating Kdp complex of Escherichia coli and is responsible
    for stabilization of the complex in vitro.
  statement: E. coli KdpF supports detergent-solubilized complex activity but was dispensable for growth
    at 0.1 mM potassium in the tested native-membrane setting.
  supporting_text: KdpF is not essential for growth on low K(+) (0.1 mM) medium
- &id011
  source_id: PMID:9099740
  title: Purification, reconstitution, and characterization of KdpD, the turgor sensor of Escherichia
    coli.
  statement: Reconstituted E. coli KdpD catalyzes autophosphorylation, phosphotransfer to KdpE and KdpE
    dephosphorylation.
  supporting_text: 'reconstituted KdpD-His6 exhibited autokinase activity, and the phosphoryl group

    could be transferred to KdpE.'
- &id013
  source_id: PMID:22291906
  title: Structure-function studies of DNA binding domain of response regulator KdpE reveals equal affinity
    interactions at DNA half-sites.
  statement: KdpE DNA recognition is necessary but an isolated DNA-binding domain is insufficient for
    transcriptional activation.
  supporting_text: 'Despite binding to these half-sites, KdpE(DBD) was

    incapable of promoting gene expression in vivo.'
- &id015
  source_id: PMID:38622146
  title: KdpD is a tandem serine histidine kinase that controls K(+) pump KdpFABC transcriptionally and
    post-translationally.
  statement: E. coli KdpD directly phosphorylates KdpB to inhibit the pump; short D. geothermalis KdpD
    retains a c-di-AMP-regulated serine-kinase mechanism without the histidine transmitter.
  supporting_text: "KdpD additionally mediates an inhibitory serine \nphosphorylation of KdpFABC at high\
    \ potassium levels"
- &id010
  source_id: PMID:39133005
  title: Regulation of potassium uptake in Caulobacter crescentus.
  statement: Native Caulobacter NA1000 supports a KdpABC/KdpE profile with conditional KdpD phosphatase-dominant
    regulation and an unidentified phosphorylation input.
  supporting_text: 'Our data therefore suggest that KdpE is

    phosphorylated by another non-cognate histidine kinase.'
- source_id: PMID:26195599
  title: Binding of Cyclic Di-AMP to the Staphylococcus aureus Sensor Kinase KdpD Occurs via the Universal
    Stress Protein Domain and Downregulates the Expression of the Kdp Potassium Transporter.
  statement: Staphylococcus KdpD c-di-AMP binding inhibits salt-induced expression of the Kdp transporter.
  supporting_text: 'c-di-AMP binding to KdpD inhibits

    the upregulation of the kdpFABC operon under salt stress'
- &id002
  source_id: PMID:41259220
  title: Conduction pathway for potassium through the Escherichia coli pump KdpFABC.
  statement: E. coli structure-function data support potassium passage from the KdpA selectivity filter
    through an inter-subunit tunnel to KdpB release sites.
  supporting_text: The results confirm that K+ ions pass through the tunnel
- &id007
  source_id: PMID:41384914
  title: On the mechanism of K+ transport through the inter-subunit tunnel of KdpFABC.
  statement: The inter-subunit tunnel is predominantly hydrated; ATPase/transport coupling at the interface
    remains mechanistically constrained rather than a settled ion-wire model.
  supporting_text: 'the tunnel is predominantly occupied by water molecules

    rather than multiple K+ ions.'
- &id005
  source_id: PMID:28636601
  title: Crystal structure of the potassium-importing KdpFABC membrane complex.
  statement: The E. coli Kdp complex joins a channel-like KdpA and P-type ATPase KdpB, with accessory
    components.
  supporting_text: 'one channel-like subunit

    (KdpA) belonging to the superfamily of potassium transporters'
- &id006
  source_id: PMID:34272288
  title: Structural basis for potassium transport in prokaryotes by KdpFABC.
  statement: E. coli cryo-EM states support KdpB conformational cycling and transfer to a cytoplasmic
    release pathway.
  supporting_text: 'This pathway runs through an intramembrane tunnel in KdpA and

    delivers ions to sites in the membrane domain of KdpB.'
notes: 'Bacteria is the distribution envelope, not a claim that every bacterium contains this system or
  the same regulatory architecture. Full matched panels are E. coli, sequence-inferred P. putida KT2440
  and experimentally studied Caulobacter NA1000. N. vulgaris KdpB is a partial pump exemplar; Staphylococcus
  and Deinococcus proteins provide regulatory comparisons rather than complete native pump witnesses.
  The regulator and pump roles require compatible proteins from a supported panel. Same-polypeptide KdpE
  receiver and DNA output, and same-panel KdpABC assembly, cannot be reconstructed by arbitrary family-hit
  mixing.


  The two pump variants preserve F-containing assembly and specifically supported F-independent capacity.
  E. coli deletion results at 0.1 mM potassium and the native Caulobacter ABC system support the latter;
  optionality is not transferred indiscriminately to every species or solubilized assay. KdpC remains
  part of the transport assembly; no independent catalytic ATPase or transporter is assigned to C or F.
  The old potassium:proton antiporter-complex mapping is not used: chemical proton bookkeeping is not
  transmembrane proton antiport.


  Canonical induction and Caulobacter regulatory profiles are alternative evidence-qualified descriptions,
  not mutually exclusive evolutionary clades. KdpD phosphatase and serine-kinase functions are distinct.
  Short KdpD proteins lacking a histidine transmitter may still retain atypical serine kinase activity.
  Caulobacter KdpE activation has an unidentified phosphorylation source; no invented kinase fills that
  gap. Dgeo serine-kinase data on the E. coli substrate do not establish a native Dgeo transport cassette.
  Regulatory capacity and active potassium flux are different endpoints; inhibitory phosphorylation can
  disable an assembled pump.


  The historical NCBIfam TIGR02115 KdpF grounding and PANTHER classifications are retained only as identity
  evidence. Broad family membership alone does not establish matched assembly, signaling specificity,
  catalytic activity, or equivalent physiological requirements. Mechanistic statements inferred from E.
  coli remain qualified in the member reviews.'

document.title: Bacterial Kdp potassium uptake and regulatory control
document.description: A bacterial potassium-homeostasis module combining the KdpABC transport machinery, a variably required KdpF stabilizing component, and lineage-dependent control of pump production and activity. KdpA selects potassium and supplies the inter-subunit pathway; KdpB couples ATP turnover to ion transfer and cytoplasmic release, supported by KdpC. Canonical KdpD-to-KdpE signaling induces pump expression, whereas a Caulobacter regulatory profile retains KdpE output without making cognate KdpD activation obligatory. Characterized KdpD proteins can also restrain KdpE phosphorylation or inhibit existing pumps through KdpB serine phosphorylation. Other potassium uptake systems and non-Kdp virulence outputs are outside this module.

document.notes:
Bacteria is the distribution envelope, not a claim that every bacterium contains this system or the same regulatory architecture. Full matched panels are E. coli, sequence-inferred P. putida KT2440 and experimentally studied Caulobacter NA1000. N. vulgaris KdpB is a partial pump exemplar; Staphylococcus and Deinococcus proteins provide regulatory comparisons rather than complete native pump witnesses. The regulator and pump roles require compatible proteins from a supported panel. Same-polypeptide KdpE receiver and DNA output, and same-panel KdpABC assembly, cannot be reconstructed by arbitrary family-hit mixing.

The two pump variants preserve F-containing assembly and specifically supported F-independent capacity. E. coli deletion results at 0.1 mM potassium and the native Caulobacter ABC system support the latter; optionality is not transferred indiscriminately to every species or solubilized assay. KdpC remains part of the transport assembly; no independent catalytic ATPase or transporter is assigned to C or F. The old potassium:proton antiporter-complex mapping is not used: chemical proton bookkeeping is not transmembrane proton antiport.

Canonical induction and Caulobacter regulatory profiles are alternative evidence-qualified descriptions, not mutually exclusive evolutionary clades. KdpD phosphatase and serine-kinase functions are distinct. Short KdpD proteins lacking a histidine transmitter may still retain atypical serine kinase activity. Caulobacter KdpE activation has an unidentified phosphorylation source; no invented kinase fills that gap. Dgeo serine-kinase data on the E. coli substrate do not establish a native Dgeo transport cassette. Regulatory capacity and active potassium flux are different endpoints; inhibitory phosphorylation can disable an assembled pump.

The historical NCBIfam TIGR02115 KdpF grounding and PANTHER classifications are retained only as identity evidence. Broad family membership alone does not establish matched assembly, signaling specificity, catalytic activity, or equivalent physiological requirements. Mechanistic statements inferred from E. coli remain qualified in the member reviews.

node.label: KdpD/KdpE phosphorelay
node.description: The sensor histidine kinase KdpD autophosphorylates in response to the potassium-limitation input and transfers phosphate directly to the conserved receiver aspartate of KdpE, which effects the transcriptional output.

references.title: Conduction pathway for potassium through the Escherichia coli pump KdpFABC.

findings.statement: E. coli structure-function data support potassium passage from the KdpA selectivity filter through an inter-subunit tunnel to KdpB release sites.
findings.supporting_text: The results confirm that K+ ions pass through the tunnel

reference_review.review_notes: Final published primary study read; use instead of older preprint as the current route evidence. No native rate or flux is transferred to other species.

references.title: On the mechanism of K+ transport through the inter-subunit tunnel of KdpFABC.

findings.statement: The inter-subunit tunnel is predominantly hydrated; ATPase/transport coupling at the interface remains mechanistically constrained rather than a settled ion-wire model.
findings.supporting_text:
the tunnel is predominantly occupied by water molecules
rather than multiple K+ ions.

reference_review.review_notes: Primary full text read. Simulations, anomalous scattering and functional assays refine microscopic coupling, without proving every proposed intermediate of the transport cycle.

references.title: Crystal structure of the potassium-importing KdpFABC membrane complex.

findings.statement: The E. coli Kdp complex joins a channel-like KdpA and P-type ATPase KdpB, with accessory components.
findings.supporting_text:
one channel-like subunit
(KdpA) belonging to the superfamily of potassium transporters

reference_review.review_notes: Primary structural evidence used for complex architecture; newer work refines the ion path. Not a direct structure of every representative.

references.title: Structural basis for potassium transport in prokaryotes by KdpFABC.

findings.statement: E. coli cryo-EM states support KdpB conformational cycling and transfer to a cytoplasmic release pathway.
findings.supporting_text:
This pathway runs through an intramembrane tunnel in KdpA and
delivers ions to sites in the membrane domain of KdpB.

reference_review.review_notes: Primary full text read. State structures support assembled-complex mechanism, not autonomous transport by either isolated A or B.
